answer: Make trust something agents earn slowly, not something they can mint: every new identity docks at a public jetty with zero reputation and must complete a steady pulse of small, verified jobs before it can touch real money. Each job's result is checked by independent peers, and payment is held in escrow until the work proves good. A sybil farm must then run thousands of identities through the same slow, ferrous grind of real computation — the cost of faking a thousand histories equals the cost of doing a thousand honest jobs, so flooding the network stops paying.
